text.content:
An elder is a vampire who has seen the passing of at least three centuries; most are of the Sixth, Seventh, or Eighth Generation. Elders are the most visible players of Camarilla politics — princes, primogen, archons, and justicars are disproportionately drawn from their ranks — though plenty prowl the fringes of Kindred society unseen. A rare few claim elder status on the strength of a powerful sire (or stolen power via diablerie) without the centuries of age to back it; these "pretenders" are grudgingly accepted for their bloodline's sake rather than their own merit.

Morality and Age

The centuries take a measurable toll on an elder's Humanity. In practical game terms, it is rare to encounter a true elder with a total of Morality Traits higher than 3. Elders on the Path of Humanity tend to retain Conviction and Self-Control rather than the gentler Traits, though Self-Control is often in short supply when an elder's pride is wounded. It is not uncommon for an ancient elder's Humanity to have eroded to only two Morality Traits, leaving her a mystery even to the ancillae and neonates she still deals with. This erosion is typically reflected outwardly as well: many elders can no longer pass for human except under carefully controlled conditions.

Character Creation

Generation is a Background Trait acquired exactly like Allies, Contacts, or Influences, so elder characters are built using the same character creation rules as any other vampire — there is no separate elder chargen track. The only exception is a Narrator/Storyteller-controlled elder built for a specific plot role.

Discipline Mastery

Elders of the Sixth and Seventh Generations can push their command of Disciplines further than younger Kindred, turning even passive powers into formidable tools through centuries of practice. Most rely on their subtler powers — particularly Dominate and Presence — to casually enforce authority over younger Kindred, reserving their most potent Discipline powers as a last resort: routine or open use of Master-level powers risks the Masquerade, reveals too much of an elder's true strength to rivals, and invites exactly the kind of attention that gets even elders destroyed. The Tremere are noted as placing unusual faith in the security their Discipline grants them, a confidence other clans regard skeptically.

Status

Status remains one of the primary currencies among elders, governing access to princes, favor with the harpies, and leverage in Elysium. Toreador elders are called out as the sect's foremost arbiters of Status, prizing style alongside substance. Temporary Status Traits are treated as too valuable to risk on uncertain outcomes.

Elder Attitudes Toward the Sabbat

Every Camarilla elder recognizes the Sabbat as an existential threat that explicitly calls for the elders' destruction. Camarilla territorial losses provoke both dread and a desire for revenge, but most elders prefer to manipulate or order younger Kindred onto the front lines rather than personally risk themselves. A minority privately believe the Camarilla's fall to the Sabbat is inevitable and quietly prepare avenues of escape rather than continuing the fight.

Relations with Neonates and Ancillae

Most elders favor rearing childer through harsh discipline and constant warnings against rebellion and the Sabbat; the Malkavian and Nosferatu are noted exceptions, favoring a lighter hand in the belief that severity only drives neonates toward the Sabbat or the anarchs. Ancillae, meanwhile, form Kindred society's fractious "middle class": individually weak, but a source of real anxiety to elders because most elders themselves rose to power through secret ancilla alliances, and fear the same being turned against them. Elders often deliberately slow the advancement of capable ancillae to keep them from accumulating power too quickly.

Elders Clan by Clan

The following are setting notes on how each clan's elders characteristically behave and what tensions define them. Not every clan is covered by the source material.

Brujah

Elder Brujah have largely abandoned rebellion for its own sake, turning instead to subverting and controlling the Camarilla from within as consummate politicians and power-brokers. This leaves them walking a tightrope: dismissed as sellouts by fiery younger Brujah, yet never fully trusted as insiders by the Camarilla's other elders. The most ancient among them still nurse the dream of a rebuilt Carthage.

Malkavian

Malkavian elders are viewed as enigmatic, wise, and dangerous, convinced that only they can properly interpret the signs and portents hidden in their fractured visions. They pay little attention to Kindred who cannot or will not see these patterns — which is to say, almost everyone else.

Nosferatu

Elder Nosferatu feel unusually uncertain and isolated at this juncture in Kindred history, distrustful even of their own younger clanmates. Their traditional patience and neutrality is fraying as the pace of change outstrips their ability to gather information carefully, leaving many gnawed by a desperation unusual for the clan.

Toreador

Elder Toreador struggle to find continued relevance for art forms they loved in life, often lashing out at talented childer for daring to walk a creative path the elders have come to see as hollow. Some, especially those with few remaining Morality Traits, indulge in increasingly degenerate behavior they excuse as artistic inspiration.

Tremere

Tremere elders' historic confidence that Thaumaturgy would guarantee their survival was badly shaken when the Assamites threw off their blood curse, leaving Tremere elders newly fearful of destruction and diablerie at Assamite hands. They face comparatively little threat from their own juniors thanks to the clan's strict internal discipline.

Ventrue

Ventrue elders see themselves as the Camarilla's stewards and feel its losses to the Sabbat as a personal failure of the other clans to pull their weight. Pride shades easily into arrogance and condescension, and some are approaching the belief that the clan may need to impose order on the rest of the sect by force.
